sources.entry: Notepad++ for Mac - Native macOS port of the Notepad++ code editor — no Wine, no emulation; runs natively on Apple Silicon and Intel Macs.

summary.one_liner: A native macOS port of the Notepad++ Windows code editor, built from the original codebase in Objective-C++ with no Wine or emulation layer.
summary.what_it_does: Nextpad++ is presented as a full native port of the Notepad++ codebase to macOS, built from source in Objective-C++ with platform-native APIs. It is distributed as a signed, notarized .dmg and can also be installed through Homebrew Cask. The README lists features including syntax highlighting for 80+ languages, multi-document tabs, split view, regex and find-in-files search, macro recording, bookmarks, code folding, and a document map. It also describes a native Plugin Admin, with about 50 plugins ported so far and about 140 expected by the end of April 2026. The UI is stated to support dark mode, a 137-language interface, and a universal binary for Apple Silicon and Intel. The project is GPL-3.0 licensed, and the README says it has no ads, subscriptions, or telemetry.
use_cases: Editing source code on a Mac with a Notepad++-style editor
Replacing Notepad++ on macOS without Wine or emulation
Comparing or editing two files side by side in split view
Searching across many files with regex
Running Notepad++ plugins and macros on a Mac
Installing a text editor via Homebrew
how_to_run: Or download the signed .dmg from nextpad.org/download or GitHub Releases
Open the .dmg and drag Nextpad++ to Applications
notable: Full port of the original Notepad++ codebase rather than a rewrite or Wine wrapper
Universal Binary with native Apple Silicon and Intel support
Apple-notarized and installable via Homebrew Cask
Native Plugin Admin with ongoing plugin porting from Windows
Uses Scintilla as the editing engine, same as the Windows version
caveats: Plugin support is incomplete: about 50 of roughly 140 plugins are ported so far
Build-from-source instructions are not yet published, so the signed .dmg or Homebrew is the practical install path
keywords: windows editor on mac without wine
